source: .github/workflows/test.yml, job `integration`, transcribed by reading the repository
constructedIndependently: Written by reading the workflow file. The inference engine was not consulted and this file is not generated from any ExecutionGraph.
cellSelection: Base matrix is os x node-version x part = 3 x 4 x 2 = 24 cells, plus 7 `include` rows. The single in-environment cell is (ubuntu-latest, 22.x, a); the rest are OUT_OF_ENVIRONMENT, recorded and not executed.
conditionsApplied: Evaluated per the workflow's own `if:` expressions for this cell, so that SKIPPED and NEVER-EXISTED stay distinguishable: the four `yarn upgrade` blocks gated on node 10.x/12.x/14.x, 16.x, 18.x and 20.x are FALSE; `yarn upgrade enhanced-resolve@...#main ...` is gated on `matrix.use_main_branches == '1'` and the BASE matrix does not declare that axis (only `include:` rows do), so it is UNDEFINED_CONTEXT, renders empty, and '' == '1' is FALSE; `yarn --frozen-lockfile` gated on node being none of 10/12/14/16/18/20/22 is FALSE for 22.x. The 22.x branch IS true and contributes two steps, since a multi-line `run:` is several commands. `yarn report:cover:merge` and Codecov follow the suite and are not on the TEST path.
compoundRunLines: Two `run:` lines are not single commands. Per docs/ci-reproduction-sample-01-amendment-3.md: `yarn link --frozen-lockfile || true` becomes a structured allowFailure step, preserving the operator's meaning without handing repository text to a shell; and `yarn cover:integration:a ... || yarn cover:integration:a ... -f` runs the FIRST command ONCE, because `-f` is jest's --onlyFailures and re-running only the failures is flake tolerance - reproducing it would let a suite that failed once be recorded as passing.
environmentNote: `steps.calculate_architecture.outputs.result` feeds setup-node's `architecture:` input. It is environment configuration produced by a third-party action, not a repository command; the canonical container is x64 and no reference step corresponds to it.

steps.evidence: ENVIRONMENT, not a workflow command. CI's actions/setup-node provisions yarn; the canonical container ships npm only. Permitted by docs/ci-reproduction-sample-01-amendment-2.md: corepack ships with node 22, only creates shims, and is recorded as an explicit environment step.
